source.text: אֶל־חִכְּךָ֣ שֹׁפָ֔ר כַּנֶּ֖שֶׁר עַל־בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה יַ֚עַן עָבְר֣וּ בְרִיתִ֔י וְעַל־תּוֹרָתִ֖י פָּשָֽׁעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: To your palate a trumpet! Like an eagle over [the] house of Yahweh, because they have transgressed my covenant, and against my instruction they have rebelled.

en.L: To your mouth a trumpet! \q Like an eagle over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q since they have transgressed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant \q and rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction.
en.B: Put the ram's horn to your lips! \q An enemy swoops like an eagle over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because they have broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant \q and rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction.
en.R: Put the trumpet to your lips! \q An enemy is swooping like an eagle over the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because the people have broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant \q and rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teaching.

es.L: ¡A tu boca la trompeta! \q Como un águila sobre la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q porque han transgredido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto \q y se han rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción.
es.B: ¡Llévate a los labios el cuerno de carnero! \q Un enemigo se lanza como un águila sobre la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q porque han quebrantado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto \q y se han rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción.
es.R: ¡Llévate la trompeta a los labios! \q Un enemigo se lanza como un águila sobre la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, \q porque el pueblo ha quebrantado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto \q y se ha rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} enseñanza.

ko.L: 네 입에 나팔을 [대어라]! \q 독수리 같은 것이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집 위에 [덮친다]. \q 그들이 내 언약을 어기고 \q 내 가르침을 거역했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 숫양 뿔 나팔을 입에 대어라! \q 적이 독수리처럼 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집을 덮친다. \q 그들이 내 언약을 깨뜨리고 \q 내 가르침을 거역했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 나팔을 입에 대고 불어라! \q 적이 독수리처럼 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집을 덮치고 있다. \q 백성이 내 언약을 깨뜨리고 \q 내 가르침을 거역했기 때문이다.

fr.L: À ta bouche, le cor ! \q Comme un aigle sur la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q parce qu’ils ont passé outre à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance \q et transgressé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} loi.
fr.B: Porte le cor à tes lèvres ! \q Un ennemi fond comme un aigle sur la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q parce qu’ils ont rompu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance \q et se sont révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} instruction.
fr.R: Porte la trompette à tes lèvres ! \q Un ennemi fond comme un aigle sur la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, \q parce que le peuple a rompu {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} alliance \q et a péché contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} enseignement.

vi.L: Hãy đặt kèn vào miệng ngươi! \q Như chim đại bàng trên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q vì chúng đã vượt qua giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và vi phạm lời dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Hãy đưa tù và lên môi! \q Kẻ thù sà xuống như chim đại bàng trên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q vì chúng đã vi phạm giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và phản nghịch lời dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Hãy đưa kèn lên môi mà thổi! \q Kẻ thù đang lao xuống như chim đại bàng trên nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, \q vì dân chúng đã vi phạm giao ước của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và chống nghịch lời dạy của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

sw.L: Baragumu kinywani mwako! \q Kama tai juu ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q kwa sababu wamelivunja agano {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} \q na kuasi dhidi ya sheria {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Weka baragumu midomoni mwako! \q Adui anashuka kama tai juu ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q kwa sababu wamevunja agano {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} \q na kuasi dhidi ya mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Weka baragumu midomoni mwako! \q Adui anashuka kwa kasi kama tai juu ya nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q kwa sababu watu wamevunja agano {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} \q na kuasi mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: a trumpet to your mouth: sound the alarm
decisions.reason: The ram's horn was blown to warn of an enemy's approach (5:8; Jeremiah 4:5; Amos 3:6). The LORD orders the prophet, or a watchman, to raise the alarm.

decisions.choice: like an eagle: an enemy swoops down on the land
alternatives: the watchman, like an eagle over the house of the LORD
decisions.reason: The line has no verb. The eagle, or vulture (the word covers both), is most likely the attacking enemy, Assyria, as in the warning of Deuteronomy 28:49: "a nation from far away ... swooping like the eagle". It could also describe the one blowing the alarm, high over the land like a bird.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the land and people that belong to the LORD
alternatives: the temple or a shrine of the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: In Hosea the LORD's "house" is the land of Israel and its people, his household (9:15). It is not the temple in Jerusalem, which stood in Judah.

decisions.choice: they have transgressed my covenant and rebelled against my instruction
decisions.reason: The first phrase is the one of 6:7. Covenant and instruction (*torah*) go together: the LORD's bond with Israel, and the teaching that tells them how to live in it. The verse names the reason for the coming attack.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, R); ram's horn (B); An enemy swoops (B, R); instruction (L, B), teaching (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for the horn and for *torah* in the prophets. Literal keeps the compressed lines with no verb; Balanced and Readable add "put" and say who comes like an eagle (m2). Readable names "the people" for "they".

decisions.choice: "trompeta" (L, R); "cuerno de carnero" (B)
decisions.reason: The shofar on its own, as the terms note sets for the Spanish prophets.

decisions.choice: "han transgredido" (L); "han quebrantado" (B, R) for the covenant
decisions.reason: As at 6:7 for the same verb.

decisions.choice: the shofar "le cor" (L, B), "la trompette" (R), throughout Hosea and Joel
decisions.reason: As the term sheet carries over from Isaiah and Jeremiah; the English has "trumpet" at Literal here, but French keeps one word per level for the instrument.

decisions.choice: *shofar* on its own: "나팔" (L, R), "숫양 뿔 나팔" (B)
decisions.reason: The wording set for the prophets when the ram's horn stands alone.

decisions.choice: *shofar* "baragumu" at every level
decisions.reason: The ram's horn keeps one Swahili word, as in 5:8, where the English varies between trumpet and ram's horn.

decisions.choice: "kèn" (L, R); "tù và" (B) for the shofar on its own
decisions.reason: The Isaiah note's wording for the shofar when no metal trumpet stands beside it, following the English "trumpet / ram's horn / trumpet".

records.literal_gloss: To me they cry, My God, we know you, Israel.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} they cry, \q "My God, we know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, [we] Israel!"
en.B: They cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q "My God, we, Israel, know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"
en.R: They cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q "My God, we, the people of Israel, know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

es.B: Claman a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}: \q «¡Dios mío, nosotros, Israel, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} conocemos!».
es.R: Claman a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}: \q «¡Dios mío, nosotros, el pueblo de Israel, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} conocemos!».

ko.L: 그들이 나에게 부르짖는다. \q "나의 하나님, 저희 이스라엘이 주님을 압니다!"
ko.B: 그들은 나에게 부르짖는다. \q "나의 하나님, 저희 이스라엘은 주님을 압니다!"
ko.R: 그들은 나에게 부르짖는다. \q "우리 하나님, 저희 이스라엘 백성은 주님을 압니다!"

fr.L: Vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ils crient : \q « Mon Dieu, nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaissons, [nous,] Israël ! »
fr.B: Ils crient vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} : \q « Mon Dieu, nous, Israël, nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaissons ! »
fr.R: Ils crient vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} : \q « Mon Dieu, nous, le peuple d’Israël, nous {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaissons ! »

vi.L: Chúng kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: \q "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con, chúng con biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, [chúng con là] Y-sơ-ra-ên!"
vi.B: Chúng kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: \q "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của con, chúng con là Y-sơ-ra-ên, chúng con biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}!"
vi.R: Chúng kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: \q "Lạy Đức Chúa Trời của chúng con, chúng con là dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, chúng con biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}!"

sw.R: Wananililia, \q "Mungu wangu, sisi watu wa Israeli tunakujua!"

decisions.choice: My God, we know you, we Israel: the people's claim
alternatives: My God, we know you! (with "Israel" as the subject of the next verse)
decisions.reason: "Israel" stands beside "we": the people name themselves as they cry out. "My God" is said by each one. They claim to know the LORD, the very thing he desires (6:6) and they said they would seek (6:3), but verse 3 shows that their claim is empty.

decisions.choice: they cry: they call for help in trouble
decisions.reason: It is the verb of 7:14, where they do not cry to the LORD from the heart. Now they cry to him with the right words, but only because trouble has come.

decisions.choice: double quotation marks; "you" in the people's words takes the setting for God
decisions.reason: The people's words are speech quoted inside the LORD's oracle, so they take double quotation marks, as in Isaiah. Readable says "the people of Israel" to make plain that the nation speaks.

decisions.choice: « » around the people's words; "te" with the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The people's cry is quoted speech inside the oracle, so it takes Spanish quotation marks; the "you" they say to God carries the setting, as in the English.

decisions.choice: The people speak to God in 합쇼체 with "저희" and "주님"
decisions.reason: People address God in 합쇼체, as in the prayers of the prophets; Korean has no deity_pronoun span for the English "You".

decisions.choice: no span on "you" in "tunakujua"
decisions.reason: The people's "you" to God is the object marker -ku-, which takes no capital; the English span has no Swahili counterpart here.

decisions.choice: the people pray with "lạy", "con", "chúng con" and "Ngài"
decisions.reason: As the Isaiah note settles for the people praying; the English deity span on "you" becomes the span on "Ngài".

records.literal_gloss: Has rejected Israel good; an enemy will pursue him.

en.L: Israel has rejected [what is] good; \q an enemy will pursue him.
en.B: Israel has rejected what is good; \q an enemy will chase him down.
en.R: But Israel has turned away from what is good, \q so an enemy will hunt them down.

es.L: Israel ha rechazado [lo] bueno; \q un enemigo lo perseguirá.
es.B: Israel ha rechazado lo que es bueno; \q un enemigo lo perseguirá hasta alcanzarlo.
es.R: Pero Israel se ha apartado de lo bueno, \q así que un enemigo los perseguirá hasta atraparlos.

ko.L: 이스라엘이 선을 버렸으니, \q 원수가 그를 뒤쫓을 것이다.
ko.B: 이스라엘이 좋은 것을 버렸으니, \q 원수가 그를 뒤쫓을 것이다.
ko.R: 그러나 이스라엘은 좋은 것에서 등을 돌렸다. \q 그래서 원수가 그들을 쫓아갈 것이다.

fr.L: Israël a rejeté [ce qui est] bon ; \q un ennemi le poursuivra.
fr.B: Israël a rejeté ce qui est bon ; \q un ennemi le pourchassera.
fr.R: Mais Israël s’est détourné de ce qui est bon, \q alors un ennemi les traquera.

vi.L: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã khước từ điều tốt; \q kẻ thù sẽ đuổi theo nó.
vi.B: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã khước từ điều tốt lành; \q kẻ thù sẽ đuổi bắt nó.
vi.R: Nhưng Y-sơ-ra-ên đã quay lưng với điều tốt lành, \q nên kẻ thù sẽ săn đuổi chúng.

sw.B: Israeli amekataa lililo jema; \q adui atamfuatia na kumkamata.
sw.R: Lakini Israeli amegeuka mbali na lililo jema, \q kwa hiyo adui atawawinda.

decisions.choice: rejected the good: turned away from the LORD's good ways
decisions.reason: "The good" may be the good the LORD gives and commands (Amos 5:14-15; Micah 6:8), or the LORD himself as the source of good (compare 3:5, "his goodness"). The verb means to cast off or spurn, and it returns in verse 5, where the calf is rejected in turn.

decisions.choice: an enemy will pursue him: the attack of verse 1
decisions.reason: The enemy is the one who swoops like an eagle in verse 1. "Him" is Israel, spoken of as one person.

decisions.choice: But ... so ... them
decisions.reason: Readable adds "but" and "so" to show the links between verses 2 and 3, and says "them" for "him", since the people are meant.

source.text: הֵ֤ם הִמְלִיכוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א מִמֶּ֔נִּי הֵשִׂ֖ירוּ וְלֹ֣א יָדָ֑עְתִּי כַּסְפָּ֣ם וּזְהָבָ֗ם עָשׂ֤וּ לָהֶם֙ עֲצַבִּ֔ים לְמַ֖עַן יִכָּרֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: They made kings, and not from me; they made officials, and not I knew; their silver and their gold they made for themselves idols, so that it will be cut off.

en.L: They made kings, but not from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q they made officials, and I did not know. \q With their silver and their gold they made idols for themselves, \q so that it will be cut off.
en.B: They set up kings, but not by {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q they appointed officials without {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} approval. \q With their silver and gold they made themselves idols, \q to their own destruction.
en.R: They put kings on the throne without asking {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They chose leaders without {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} approval. \q They used their silver and gold to make idols, \q and that will bring their ruin.

es.L: Ellos pusieron reyes, pero no de parte {{deity_pronoun:mía|Mía}}; \q pusieron príncipes, y yo no lo supe. \q Con su plata y su oro se hicieron ídolos, \q para ser destruidos.
es.B: Pusieron reyes, pero no por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; \q nombraron jefes sin {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} aprobación. \q Con su plata y su oro se hicieron ídolos, \q para su propia destrucción.
es.R: Pusieron reyes en el trono, y a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} preguntaron. \q Escogieron dirigentes sin {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} aprobación. \q Usaron su plata y su oro para hacer ídolos, \q y eso los llevará a la ruina.

ko.L: 그들이 왕들을 세웠으나 나로 말미암은 것이 아니고, \q 고관들을 세웠으나 나는 알지 못했다. \q 그들이 자기 은과 금으로 자기들을 위해 우상들을 만들었으니, \q 그것은 끊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 그들이 왕들을 세웠으나 내가 세운 것이 아니고, \q 관리들을 세웠으나 내가 허락한 것이 아니다. \q 그들은 자기 은과 금으로 우상들을 만들었으니, \q 그것이 그들의 멸망을 부를 것이다.
ko.R: 그들은 나에게 묻지도 않고 왕들을 세웠다. \q 내가 허락하지도 않았는데 지도자들을 뽑았다. \q 그들은 은과 금으로 우상들을 만들었다. \q 그 일이 그들을 망하게 할 것이다.

fr.L: Ils ont fait des rois, mais pas de par {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q ils ont fait des chefs, et je ne l’ai pas su. \q De leur argent et de leur or ils se sont fait des idoles, \q pour qu’il soit retranché.
fr.B: Ils ont établi des rois, mais sans {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q ils ont nommé des chefs sans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} accord. \q Avec leur argent et leur or ils se sont fait des idoles, \q pour leur propre ruine.
fr.R: Ils ont mis des rois sur le trône sans {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} consulter. \q Ils ont choisi des dirigeants sans {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} accord. \q Ils ont pris leur argent et leur or pour faire des idoles, \q et cela causera leur ruine.

vi.L: Chúng đã lập vua, nhưng không bởi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q chúng đã lập quan chức, mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không biết. \q Bằng bạc và vàng của chúng, chúng làm thần tượng cho mình, \q để rồi nó bị diệt mất.
vi.B: Chúng lập vua, nhưng không do {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q chúng bổ nhiệm quan chức mà không được {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chấp thuận. \q Chúng lấy bạc vàng làm thần tượng cho mình, \q để tự chuốc lấy sự hủy diệt.
vi.R: Chúng đưa người lên làm vua mà không hỏi ý {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Chúng chọn người lãnh đạo mà không được {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chấp thuận. \q Chúng dùng bạc vàng của mình làm thần tượng, \q và điều đó sẽ đem lại sự sụp đổ cho chúng.

sw.L: Wamejifanyia wafalme, lakini si kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}; \q wameweka wakuu, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} sikujua. \q Kwa fedha yao na dhahabu yao wamejifanyia sanamu, \q ili ikatiliwe mbali.
sw.B: Wamewaweka wafalme, lakini si {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyewaweka; \q wamewachagua wakuu bila idhini {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Kwa fedha na dhahabu yao wamejitengenezea sanamu, \q kwa maangamizi yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Wamewaweka wafalme bila kuniuliza. \q Wamewachagua viongozi bila idhini {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Wametumia fedha na dhahabu yao kutengeneza sanamu, \q na jambo hilo litawaletea maangamizi.

decisions.choice: they made kings, but not from me: kings set up by plotters, not chosen by the LORD
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom's last kings came to the throne by murder (7:3-7; 2 Kings 15:8-30). The words may also look back to the north's break from David's house (1 Kings 12:16-20), though that was foretold by a prophet (1 Kings 11:29-31). The point is that Israel did not ask the LORD.

decisions.choice: I did not know: without my approval
decisions.reason: To "know" here is to acknowledge or approve. The officials were appointed without the LORD's consent.

decisions.choice: so that it will be cut off: with destruction as the result
alternatives: so that he (Israel) will be cut off
decisions.reason: The small word usually expresses purpose, but here it gives the result: all that silver and gold ends in destruction. What will be cut off is not named; it may be the silver and gold, or Israel itself.

decisions.choice: without my approval (B, R); to their own destruction (B); that will bring their ruin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "I did not know" (m2), and of the last phrase (m3).

source.text: זָנַח֙ עֶגְלֵ֣ךְ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן חָרָ֥ה אַפִּ֖י בָּ֑ם עַד־מָתַ֕י לֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ נִקָּיֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: He has rejected your calf, Samaria; my anger burns against them; until when will they not be able [to attain] innocence?

en.L: He has rejected your calf, Samaria; \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger burns against them; \q until when will they be unable [to attain] innocence?
en.B: Your calf is rejected, Samaria! \q My anger burns against them. \q How long will they be unable to become clean?
en.R: Samaria, your calf-idol is rejected! \q I am furious with the people. \q How long will it be before they can be free from guilt?

es.L: Él ha rechazado tu becerro, Samaria; \q {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira arde contra ellos; \q ¿hasta cuándo serán incapaces de [alcanzar] la inocencia?
es.B: ¡Tu becerro ha sido rechazado, Samaria! \q Mi ira arde contra ellos. \q ¿Hasta cuándo seguirán sin poder purificarse?
es.R: ¡Samaria, tu becerro-ídolo ha sido rechazado! \q Estoy furioso con el pueblo. \q ¿Cuánto tiempo pasará antes de que puedan quedar libres de culpa?

ko.L: 사마리아야, 그분께서 네 송아지를 버리셨다. \q 내 진노가 그들을 향해 불타오른다. \q 그들이 언제까지 깨끗함에 [이르지] 못하겠느냐?
ko.B: 사마리아야, 네 송아지는 버림받았다! \q 내 진노가 그들을 향해 불타오른다. \q 그들이 언제까지 깨끗해지지 못하겠느냐?
ko.R: 사마리아야, 네 송아지 우상은 버림받았다! \q 나는 백성에게 몹시 화가 나 있다. \q 그들이 언제쯤에야 죄에서 깨끗해지겠느냐?

fr.L: Il a rejeté ton veau, Samarie ; \q {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère s’enflamme contre eux ; \q jusqu’à quand seront-ils incapables d’[atteindre] l’innocence ?
fr.B: Ton veau est rejeté, Samarie ! \q Ma colère s’enflamme contre eux. \q Jusqu’à quand seront-ils incapables de devenir purs ?
fr.R: Samarie, ton idole en forme de veau est rejetée ! \q Je suis furieux contre le peuple. \q Combien de temps faudra-t-il encore avant qu’ils soient libérés de leur culpabilité ?

vi.L: Ngài đã khước từ con bò con của ngươi, hỡi Sa-ma-ri; \q cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nổi phừng nghịch cùng chúng; \q cho đến bao giờ chúng mới có thể [được] trong sạch?
vi.B: Hỡi Sa-ma-ri, con bò con của ngươi đã bị khước từ! \q Cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nổi phừng nghịch cùng chúng. \q Cho đến bao giờ chúng mới có thể trở nên trong sạch?
vi.R: Hỡi Sa-ma-ri, tượng bò con của ngươi đã bị loại bỏ! \q Ta rất giận dân này. \q Phải đến bao giờ chúng mới được sạch tội?

sw.L: Amemkataa ndama wako, Samaria; \q hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} inawaka dhidi yao; \q mpaka lini hawataweza [kufikia] kutokuwa na hatia?
sw.B: Ndama wako amekataliwa, Samaria! \q Hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} inawaka dhidi yao. \q Mpaka lini hawataweza kuwa safi?
sw.R: Samaria, sanamu yako ya ndama imekataliwa! \q Nimewakasirikia watu sana. \q Itachukua muda gani mpaka waweze kuwa huru na hatia?

decisions.choice: he has rejected your calf: the calf is rejected by the LORD
alternatives: your calf has rejected you, Samaria
decisions.reason: The verb is the one of verse 3: Israel rejected the good, and now the calf is rejected. The Hebrew says "he has rejected", without naming who; it is the LORD, though he speaks of himself as "my" in the next line. The words can also be read "your calf has rejected you", or as a command, "Reject your calf!". Some ancient versions read "I have rejected".

decisions.choice: your calf, Samaria: the golden calf worshiped in the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Jeroboam I set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan, saying "Here are your gods, Israel" (1 Kings 12:28-30). Samaria, the capital, stands for the whole kingdom. Hosea mocks the calf of Beth-aven, that is Bethel, in 10:5.

decisions.choice: innocence: cleanness from guilt
decisions.reason: The word means being clean or free of guilt (Genesis 20:5; Psalm 26:6). The question asks how long Israel will be unable to give up its idols and be clean.

decisions.choice: Your calf is rejected (B, R); calf-idol (R); I am furious (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "is rejected", so that the change from "he" to "my" does not confuse the reader; the one who rejects is the LORD (m1). Readable says "calf-idol" and turns "my anger burns" into "I am furious".

decisions.choice: "tu becerro" (L, B); "tu becerro-ídolo" (R)
decisions.reason: The calf image as the Spanish Kings has it (1 Kings 12:28 "becerros"); Samaria is spoken to as tú.

decisions.choice: "그분께서 … 버리셨다" (L), with the honorific
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he has rejected" refers to the LORD in the third person; the shared footnote reads it so, and Korean gives the honorific as it does wherever the English uses a deity span or God is spoken of. B and R use the passive, as the English.

source.text: כִּ֤י מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְה֔וּא חָרָ֣שׁ עָשָׂ֔הוּ וְלֹ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים ה֑וּא כִּֽי־שְׁבָבִ֣ים יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עֵ֖גֶל שֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: For from Israel [is] even it; a craftsman made it, and not God [is] it; for splinters will become [the] calf of Samaria.

en.L: For from Israel [is] even this; \q a craftsman made it, \q and it [is] not God; \q for the calf of Samaria will become splinters.
en.B: This thing too comes from Israel: \q a craftsman made it; \q it is not God. \q The calf of Samaria will be smashed to splinters.
en.R: This calf came from Israel itself. \q A craftsman made it. \q It is not God! \q The calf of Samaria will be smashed to pieces.

es.L: Porque de Israel [es] también este; \q un artesano lo hizo, \q y no [es] Dios; \q por eso el becerro de Samaria será hecho astillas.
es.B: También esto viene de Israel: \q un artesano lo hizo; \q no es Dios. \q El becerro de Samaria será hecho astillas.
es.R: Este becerro salió del mismo Israel. \q Un artesano lo hizo. \q ¡No es Dios! \q El becerro de Samaria será hecho pedazos.

ko.L: 이것도 이스라엘에게서 [나왔다]. \q 장인이 그것을 만들었으니, \q 그것은 신이 아니다. \q 사마리아의 송아지는 산산조각이 날 것이다.
ko.B: 이것도 이스라엘이 만든 것이다. \q 장인이 그것을 만들었으니, \q 그것은 하나님이 아니다. \q 사마리아의 송아지는 산산조각이 날 것이다.
ko.R: 이 송아지는 이스라엘 사람이 만든 것이다. \q 기술자가 그것을 만들었다. \q 그것은 하나님이 아니다! \q 사마리아의 송아지는 박살이 날 것이다.

fr.L: Car il vient d’Israël, lui aussi ; \q un artisan l’a fait, \q et il n’est pas Dieu ; \q car le veau de Samarie deviendra des éclats.
fr.B: Lui aussi vient d’Israël : \q un artisan l’a fabriqué ; \q ce n’est pas Dieu. \q Le veau de Samarie sera réduit en éclats.
fr.R: Ce veau vient d’Israël lui-même. \q Un artisan l’a fabriqué. \q Ce n’est pas Dieu ! \q Le veau de Samarie sera réduit en morceaux.

vi.L: Vì ngay cả nó cũng từ Y-sơ-ra-ên mà ra; \q một người thợ đã làm ra nó, \q và nó không phải là Đức Chúa Trời; \q vì con bò con của Sa-ma-ri sẽ thành ra mảnh vụn.
vi.B: Vật này cũng từ Y-sơ-ra-ên mà ra: \q một người thợ đã làm ra nó; \q nó không phải là Đức Chúa Trời. \q Con bò con của Sa-ma-ri sẽ bị đập vỡ thành mảnh vụn.
vi.R: Tượng bò con này do chính Y-sơ-ra-ên làm ra. \q Một người thợ đã làm ra nó. \q Nó không phải là Đức Chúa Trời! \q Tượng bò con của Sa-ma-ri sẽ bị đập tan thành từng mảnh.

sw.L: Kwa maana hata huyu [ni] kutoka Israeli; \q fundi alimtengeneza, \q naye si Mungu; \q kwa maana ndama wa Samaria atakuwa vipande vipande.
sw.B: Huyu naye anatoka Israeli: \q fundi alimtengeneza; \q si Mungu. \q Ndama wa Samaria atavunjwa vipande vipande.
sw.R: Ndama huyu alitoka Israeli yenyewe. \q Fundi alimtengeneza. \q Huyo si Mungu! \q Ndama wa Samaria atavunjwa vipande vipande.

decisions.choice: from Israel is even this: the calf is Israel's own work
decisions.reason: The calf did not come from heaven but from Israel: a human craftsman made it, so it cannot be God (compare Isaiah 44:9-20; Hosea 13:2). The Hebrew is short and can be joined to the end of verse 5: "How long ... ? For it is from Israel."

decisions.choice: splinters: broken pieces
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It probably means splinters or broken pieces, so the calf will be smashed to bits, as Moses destroyed the golden calf at Sinai (Exodus 32:20).

decisions.choice: comes from Israel (B, R); smashed to splinters (B); smashed to pieces (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the first line in plain order, and say how the calf will become splinters.

source.text: כִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ יִזְרָ֖עוּ וְסוּפָ֣תָה יִקְצֹ֑רוּ קָמָ֣ה אֵֽין־ל֗וֹ צֶ֚מַח בְּלִ֣י יַֽעֲשֶׂה־קֶּ֔מַח אוּלַ֣י יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה זָרִ֖ים יִבְלָעֻֽהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For wind they sow, and whirlwind they reap; standing grain, no head to it; it will not yield flour; if it should yield, strangers would swallow it.

en.L: For they sow wind, and they reap whirlwind; \q standing grain has no head; it will not yield flour; \q if it should yield, \q strangers would swallow it up.
en.B: They sow the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind. \q The standing grain has no head; it will make no flour. \q Even if it did, \q foreigners would swallow it up.
en.R: They plant the wind, and they will harvest the whirlwind. \q Their grain will have no heads, and it will make no flour. \q And if it did make any, \q foreigners would eat it all.

es.L: Porque siembran viento, y cosechan torbellino; \q la mies no tiene espiga; no dará harina; \q y si la diera, \q extraños la devorarían.
es.B: Siembran viento y cosecharán torbellino. \q El trigo en pie no tiene espiga; no dará harina. \q Y aunque la diera, \q los extranjeros se la tragarían.
es.R: Plantan el viento, y cosecharán el torbellino. \q Su trigo no tendrá espigas, y no dará harina. \q Y si diera algo, \q los extranjeros se lo comerían todo.

ko.L: 그들이 바람을 심고 회오리바람을 거둔다. \q 서 있는 곡식에 이삭이 없으니, 가루를 내지 못할 것이다. \q 혹시 낸다 해도 \q 이방인들이 그것을 삼킬 것이다.
ko.B: 그들은 바람을 심고 회오리바람을 거둘 것이다. \q 곡식 줄기에 이삭이 없으니 가루를 내지 못한다. \q 설령 낸다 해도 \q 이방인들이 그것을 삼켜 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그들은 바람을 심었으니 회오리바람을 거둘 것이다. \q 그들의 곡식에는 이삭이 없어서 밀가루를 만들지 못할 것이다. \q 혹시 조금 만든다 해도 \q 다른 나라 사람들이 다 먹어 버릴 것이다.

fr.L: Car ils sèment le vent, et ils moissonnent le tourbillon ; \q le blé sur pied n’a pas d’épi ; il ne donnera pas de farine ; \q s’il en donnait, \q des étrangers l’engloutiraient.
fr.B: Ils sèment le vent, et ils récolteront la tempête. \q Le blé sur pied n’a pas d’épi ; il ne donnera pas de farine. \q Et même s’il en donnait, \q des étrangers l’engloutiraient.
fr.R: Ils plantent le vent, et ils récolteront la tempête. \q Leur blé n’aura pas d’épis, et il ne donnera pas de farine. \q Et s’il en donnait un peu, \q des étrangers mangeraient tout.

vi.L: Vì chúng gieo gió, và chúng gặt bão lốc; \q lúa đứng không có bông; nó sẽ không cho bột; \q nếu có cho, \q người ngoại bang sẽ nuốt mất.
vi.B: Chúng gieo gió thì sẽ gặt bão. \q Lúa đứng không trổ bông, sẽ chẳng làm ra bột. \q Mà dù có làm ra, \q người ngoại quốc cũng sẽ nuốt mất.
vi.R: Chúng gieo gió thì sẽ gặt bão. \q Lúa của chúng sẽ không có bông, và sẽ không làm ra bột. \q Mà nếu có làm ra chút nào, \q người ngoại quốc cũng sẽ ăn hết.

sw.L: Kwa maana wanapanda upepo, nao wanavuna kimbunga; \q bua lililosimama halina suke; halitatoa unga; \q hata likitoa, \q wageni wangeumeza.
sw.B: Wanapanda upepo, nao watavuna kimbunga. \q Bua lililosimama halina suke; halitatoa unga. \q Hata kama lingetoa, \q wageni wangeumeza.
sw.R: Wanapanda upepo, nao watavuna dhoruba kali. \q Nafaka yao haitakuwa na masuke, wala haitatoa unga. \q Na hata kama ingetoa, \q wageni wangeula wote.

decisions.choice: they sow the wind and reap the whirlwind: empty deeds bring a far worse harvest
decisions.reason: What they sow is wind: nothing, worthless things such as the calf and the alliances with foreign powers (12:2, "Ephraim feeds on the wind"). What they reap is the whirlwind, a storm of destruction far greater than what was sown. The saying rests on the farmer's rule that a person reaps what is sown (10:12-13; Job 4:8; Proverbs 22:8; Galatians 6:7). It has become a proverb in many languages.

decisions.choice: whirlwind: a violent storm wind
decisions.reason: The word is used of the storm that sweeps everything away (Proverbs 1:27; 10:25), and of the LORD coming in judgment (Isaiah 66:15; Nahum 1:3). The form here has an old ending that adds weight to the word.

decisions.choice: no head, no flour: a sound play in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The words for "head" (of grain) and "flour" sound alike in Hebrew, so the line rings like a saying: the stalk grows no head, the head gives no flour. Their harvest fails, and even if it yielded something, foreigners would take it, through war and tribute (7:9).

decisions.choice: strangers would swallow it up
decisions.reason: "Strangers" are the foreign nations, as in 7:9. "Swallow up" leads into verse 8, where Israel itself is swallowed up.

decisions.choice: sow the wind ... reap the whirlwind (B); plant the wind ... harvest the whirlwind (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew's picture in the words that English already uses for it, with "the" before both nouns and "will reap" for the harvest still to come. Readable says "plant" and "harvest", and "eat it all" for "swallow it up". The sound play of the second line cannot be kept (m3).

decisions.choice: "le tourbillon" (L), "la tempête" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal names the whirling storm wind; Balanced and Readable use "la tempête", the word French already pairs with sowing the wind, so the saying is heard.

decisions.choice: the sound play "no head, no flour" not kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew *tsemach* / *qemach* (m3) has no Swahili equivalent; the footnote explains it.

decisions.choice: "gieo gió thì sẽ gặt bão" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese already has this verse as a proverb, "gieo gió gặt bão", so Balanced and Readable use its familiar shape; Literal keeps "bão lốc" for the whirlwind.

source.text: נִבְלַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַתָּה֙ הָי֣וּ בַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּכְלִ֖י אֵֽין־חֵ֥פֶץ בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Swallowed up is Israel; now they have become among the nations like a vessel [in which there is] no delight in it.

en.L: Israel is swallowed up; \q now they have become among the nations \q like a vessel no one delights in.
en.B: Israel has been swallowed up; \q now they are among the nations \q like a jar that no one wants.
en.R: Israel has been swallowed up. \q Now the people live among the nations \q like a jar that no one wants anymore.

es.L: Israel es devorado; \q ahora están entre las naciones \q como una vasija que nadie aprecia.
es.B: Israel ha sido devorado; \q ahora está entre las naciones \q como un cántaro que nadie quiere.
es.R: Israel ha sido devorado. \q Ahora el pueblo vive entre las naciones \q como un cántaro que ya nadie quiere.

ko.L: 이스라엘이 삼켜졌다. \q 이제 그들이 민족들 가운데서 \q 아무도 좋아하지 않는 그릇처럼 되었다.
ko.B: 이스라엘은 삼켜졌다. \q 이제 그들은 민족들 가운데서 \q 아무도 원하지 않는 그릇과 같다.
ko.R: 이스라엘은 삼켜져 버렸다. \q 이제 백성은 다른 민족들 가운데서 \q 아무도 쓰지 않는 그릇처럼 살고 있다.

fr.L: Israël est englouti ; \q maintenant ils sont devenus parmi les nations \q comme un vase auquel personne ne prend plaisir.
fr.B: Israël a été englouti ; \q maintenant ils sont parmi les nations \q comme une jarre dont personne ne veut.
fr.R: Israël a été englouti. \q Maintenant le peuple vit parmi les nations \q comme une jarre dont plus personne ne veut.

vi.L: Y-sơ-ra-ên bị nuốt mất; \q bây giờ chúng đã trở nên giữa các nước \q như một cái bình không ai ưa thích.
vi.B: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã bị nuốt mất; \q bây giờ chúng ở giữa các nước \q như một cái bình không ai muốn dùng.
vi.R: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã bị nuốt mất. \q Bây giờ dân ấy sống giữa các nước \q như một cái bình không còn ai muốn dùng nữa.

sw.L: Israeli amemezwa; \q sasa wamekuwa kati ya mataifa \q kama chombo kisichopendezwa na mtu.
sw.B: Israeli amemezwa; \q sasa wako kati ya mataifa \q kama chungu ambacho hakuna anayekitaka.
sw.R: Israeli amemezwa. \q Sasa watu wanaishi kati ya mataifa \q kama chungu ambacho hakuna anayekitaka tena.

decisions.choice: Israel is swallowed up; now they are among the nations
decisions.reason: The foreigners who would swallow the grain (verse 7) swallow Israel itself. "Now" speaks of it as already happening: Israel has lost its freedom to Assyria, and in Hosea's time the Assyrians had already carried off people from Galilee and Gilead (2 Kings 15:29).

decisions.choice: a vessel no one delights in: something thrown away as worthless
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses the same words of King Coniah (Jeremiah 22:28) and of Moab (Jeremiah 48:38). A cheap clay jar that no one wants is thrown out.

decisions.choice: a vessel no one delights in (L); a jar that no one wants (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Jeremiah 22:28 and 48:38 at each level, where the Hebrew is the same. Readable says "the people" for "they" and "live among" for "have become among".

source.text: כִּֽי־הֵ֨מָּה֙ עָל֣וּ אַשּׁ֔וּר פֶּ֖רֶא בּוֹדֵ֣ד ל֑וֹ אֶפְרַ֖יִם הִתְנ֥וּ אֲהָבִֽים

records.literal_gloss: For they have gone up [to] Assyria, a wild donkey alone by itself; Ephraim has hired lovers.

en.L: For they have gone up [to] Assyria, \q a wild donkey alone by itself; \q Ephraim has hired lovers.
en.B: They have gone up to Assyria, \q like a wild donkey roaming on its own. \q Ephraim has paid for lovers.
en.R: They have gone to Assyria for help, \q like a wild donkey that wanders off alone. \q Ephraim has paid other nations to be his lovers.

es.L: Porque han subido [a] Asiria, \q un asno salvaje solitario; \q Efraín ha alquilado amantes.
es.B: Han subido a Asiria, \q como un asno salvaje que anda solo. \q Efraín ha pagado por amantes.
es.R: Han ido a Asiria a pedir ayuda, \q como un asno salvaje que se va solo por su cuenta. \q Efraín ha pagado a otras naciones para que sean sus amantes.

ko.L: 그들이 앗시리아로 올라갔다. \q 홀로 떨어져 다니는 들나귀처럼. \q 에브라임이 애인들을 샀다.
ko.B: 그들은 앗시리아로 올라갔다. \q 홀로 떠돌아다니는 들나귀처럼 갔다. \q 에브라임은 돈을 주고 애인들을 샀다.
ko.R: 그들은 도움을 얻으려고 앗시리아로 갔다. \q 혼자 떠돌아다니는 들나귀처럼 갔다. \q 에브라임은 다른 나라들에게 돈을 주고 자기 애인이 되게 했다.

fr.L: Car ils sont montés [vers] l’Assyrie, \q âne sauvage seul à l’écart ; \q Éphraïm a loué des amants.
fr.B: Ils sont montés vers l’Assyrie, \q comme un âne sauvage qui va seul de son côté. \q Éphraïm a payé des amants.
fr.R: Ils sont allés chercher de l’aide en Assyrie, \q comme un âne sauvage qui s’en va tout seul. \q Éphraïm a payé d’autres nations pour en faire ses amants.

vi.L: Vì chúng đã đi lên A-si-ri, \q một con lừa rừng đơn độc một mình; \q Ép-ra-im đã thuê tình nhân.
vi.B: Chúng đã đi lên A-si-ri, \q như con lừa rừng đi lang thang một mình. \q Ép-ra-im đã bỏ tiền mua tình nhân.
vi.R: Chúng đã đến A-si-ri cầu cứu, \q như con lừa rừng đi lạc một mình. \q Ép-ra-im đã trả tiền cho các nước khác để họ làm tình nhân của nó.

sw.L: Kwa maana wamepanda [kwenda] Ashuru, \q punda-mwitu aliye peke yake; \q Efraimu amejiajiria wapenzi.
sw.B: Wamepanda kwenda Ashuru, \q kama punda-mwitu anayetangatanga peke yake. \q Efraimu amewalipa wapenzi.
sw.R: Wamekwenda Ashuru kutafuta msaada, \q kama punda-mwitu anayejiendea peke yake. \q Efraimu amewalipa mataifa mengine ili wawe wapenzi wake.

decisions.choice: a wild donkey alone: stubborn and going its own way, with a play on Ephraim's name
alternatives: even a wild donkey keeps to itself, but Ephraim hires lovers
decisions.reason: The wild donkey roams the desert alone and will not be tamed (Genesis 16:12; Job 39:5-8; Jeremiah 2:24). The Hebrew word for it sounds like "Ephraim". The line may compare Ephraim to the donkey, or set them apart: even a wild donkey keeps to itself, but Ephraim goes looking for lovers.

decisions.choice: hired lovers: paid for alliances with foreign powers
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for a prostitute's pay (2:14; 9:1). Ephraim is pictured as a woman who pays her lovers, which is worse than taking pay (Ezekiel 16:33-34). The lovers are foreign nations, bought with tribute, as when Menahem paid the king of Assyria (2 Kings 15:19-20).

decisions.choice: gone up to Assyria: gone to seek its help
decisions.reason: To go up to a king is to go to his court. Israel's kings sent to Assyria for support (7:11; 2 Kings 15:19-20; 17:3).

decisions.choice: like a wild donkey (B, R); for help (R); paid other nations to be his lovers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "like", taking the donkey as a picture of Ephraim (m1). Readable says why they went to Assyria and who the lovers are (m2).

source.text: גַּ֛ם כִּֽי־יִתְנ֥וּ בַגּוֹיִ֖ם עַתָּ֣ה אֲקַבְּצֵ֑ם וַיָּחֵ֣לּוּ מְּעָ֔ט מִמַּשָּׂ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ שָׂרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Even though they hire among the nations, now I will gather them; and they have begun a little from [the] burden of [the] king of officials.

en.L: Even though they hire [lovers] among the nations, now I will gather them up; \q and they will begin, in a little while, [to suffer] \q under the burden of the king of princes.
en.B: Even though they hire lovers among the nations, I will now gather them together, \q and soon they will begin to suffer \q under the burden of the king of princes.
en.R: Even though they pay the nations to be their lovers, I will now gather them up. \q Soon they will start to suffer \q under the heavy load put on them by the king of princes.

es.L: Aunque alquilen [amantes] entre las naciones, ahora los reuniré; \q y comenzarán dentro de poco [a sufrir] \q bajo la carga del rey de príncipes.
es.B: Aunque alquilen amantes entre las naciones, ahora los reuniré, \q y pronto comenzarán a sufrir \q bajo la carga del rey de príncipes.
es.R: Aunque paguen a las naciones para que sean sus amantes, ahora los reuniré. \q Pronto comenzarán a sufrir \q bajo la pesada carga que les pondrá el rey de príncipes.

ko.L: 그들이 민족들 가운데서 [애인들을] 사더라도, 이제 내가 그들을 모으겠다. \q 그들이 머지않아 [괴로움을 겪기] 시작할 것이다. \q 고관들의 왕이 지우는 짐 때문이다.
ko.B: 그들이 민족들 가운데서 애인들을 사더라도, 이제 내가 그들을 한데 모으겠다. \q 그들은 곧 괴로움을 겪기 시작할 것이다. \q 고관들의 왕이 지우는 짐에 짓눌릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그들이 다른 나라들에게 돈을 주고 애인이 되게 하더라도, 이제 나는 그들을 모아들이겠다. \q 그들은 곧 고통을 겪기 시작할 것이다. \q 고관들의 왕이 그들에게 무거운 짐을 지울 것이다.

fr.L: Même s’ils louent [des amants] parmi les nations, maintenant je les rassemblerai ; \q et ils commenceront, dans peu [de temps, à souffrir] \q sous le fardeau du roi des princes.
fr.B: Même s’ils louent des amants parmi les nations, je vais maintenant les rassembler, \q et bientôt ils commenceront à souffrir \q sous le fardeau du roi des princes.
fr.R: Même s’ils paient les nations pour en faire leurs amants, je vais maintenant les rassembler. \q Bientôt ils commenceront à souffrir \q sous la lourde charge que leur imposera le roi des princes.

vi.L: Dù chúng thuê [tình nhân] giữa các nước, bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ gom chúng lại; \q và chẳng bao lâu nữa chúng sẽ bắt đầu [đau khổ] \q dưới gánh nặng của vua các vương hầu.
vi.B: Dù chúng thuê tình nhân giữa các nước, bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ gom chúng lại, \q và chẳng bao lâu chúng sẽ bắt đầu đau khổ \q dưới gánh nặng của vua các vương hầu.
vi.R: Dù chúng trả tiền cho các nước để làm tình nhân của chúng, bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ gom chúng lại. \q Chẳng bao lâu chúng sẽ bắt đầu khốn khổ \q dưới gánh nặng mà vua của các vương hầu đặt trên chúng.

sw.L: Ingawa wanaajiri [wapenzi] kati ya mataifa, sasa nitawakusanya; \q nao wataanza kidogo [kuteseka] \q chini ya mzigo wa mfalme wa wakuu.
sw.B: Ingawa wanajiajiria wapenzi kati ya mataifa, sasa nitawakusanya pamoja, \q na hivi karibuni wataanza kuteseka \q chini ya mzigo wa mfalme wa wakuu.
sw.R: Ingawa wanayalipa mataifa ili yawe wapenzi wao, sasa nitawakusanya. \q Hivi karibuni wataanza kuteseka \q chini ya mzigo mzito watakaotwikwa na mfalme wa wakuu.

decisions.choice: I will gather them; they will soon begin to suffer
alternatives: they will soon writhe under the burden
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this verse is hard. "Gather them" may mean gather Israel for judgment (as 9:6) or gather the nations against them. The next verb most likely means "they have begun" or "they will begin", with the rest left unsaid; with other vowels it can mean "they will writhe" or "they will be few". The Greek translation reads the line quite differently: "they will cease for a little while from anointing a king and princes".

decisions.choice: the burden of the king of princes: the tribute laid on Israel by the king of Assyria
alternatives: the burden of king and princes (Israel's own rulers)
decisions.reason: "King of princes" is likely a title of the Assyrian king, whose officers were themselves rulers (Isaiah 10:8; compare "king of kings", Ezekiel 26:7). The burden is the heavy tribute he demanded (2 Kings 15:19-20). The words can also be read "king and princes", Israel's own rulers, as in 3:4 and 7:3.

decisions.choice: [lovers], [to suffer] (L); lovers, to suffer (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verbs "hire" and "begin" have no object in the Hebrew. Literal brackets the words that complete them, following verse 9 and m1; Balanced and Readable supply them without brackets.

decisions.choice: "vua các vương hầu"
decisions.reason: The Assyrian title, "king of princes", is rendered with "vương hầu" (princes, vassal rulers), which carries the royal sense better than the usual "quan chức" for sarim.

source.text: כִּֽי־הִרְבָּ֥ה אֶפְרַ֛יִם מִזְבְּחֹ֖ת לַחֲטֹ֑א הָיוּ־ל֥וֹ מִזְבְּח֖וֹת לַחֲטֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: For has multiplied Ephraim altars for sin; they have become to him altars for sinning.

en.L: For Ephraim has multiplied altars for sin; \q they have become to him altars for sinning.
en.B: Ephraim has built many altars for sin, \q but they have become altars for sinning.
en.R: Ephraim has built more and more altars to take away sin, \q but those altars have become places for sinning.

es.L: Porque Efraín ha multiplicado altares para pecado; \q se le han vuelto altares para pecar.
es.B: Efraín ha construido muchos altares para el pecado, \q pero se le han vuelto altares para pecar.
es.R: Efraín ha construido más y más altares para quitar el pecado, \q pero esos altares se han vuelto lugares para pecar.

ko.L: 에브라임이 죄를 위하여 제단을 많이 만들었으나, \q 그것들이 그에게 죄를 짓는 제단이 되었다.
ko.B: 에브라임이 죄를 없애려고 제단을 많이 쌓았으나, \q 그 제단들은 죄를 짓는 곳이 되고 말았다.
ko.R: 에브라임은 죄를 없애려고 제단을 점점 더 많이 쌓았다. \q 그러나 그 제단들은 죄를 짓는 곳이 되었다.

fr.L: Car Éphraïm a multiplié les autels pour le péché ; \q ils sont devenus pour lui des autels pour pécher.
fr.B: Éphraïm a construit beaucoup d’autels pour le péché, \q mais ils sont devenus des autels pour pécher.
fr.R: Éphraïm a construit de plus en plus d’autels pour enlever le péché, \q mais ces autels sont devenus des endroits où l’on pèche.

vi.L: Vì Ép-ra-im đã làm thêm nhiều bàn thờ [dâng tế lễ] chuộc tội; \q chúng đã trở nên những bàn thờ để phạm tội cho nó.
vi.B: Ép-ra-im đã xây nhiều bàn thờ để chuộc tội, \q nhưng chúng lại trở thành bàn thờ để phạm tội.
vi.R: Ép-ra-im đã xây ngày càng nhiều bàn thờ để xóa tội, \q nhưng những bàn thờ ấy lại trở thành nơi để phạm tội.

sw.L: Kwa maana Efraimu ameongeza madhabahu kwa ajili ya dhambi; \q zimekuwa kwake madhabahu za kutenda dhambi.
sw.B: Efraimu amejenga madhabahu nyingi kwa ajili ya dhambi, \q lakini zimekuwa madhabahu za kutenda dhambi.
sw.R: Efraimu amejenga madhabahu zaidi na zaidi ili kuondoa dhambi, \q lakini madhabahu hizo zimekuwa mahali pa kutenda dhambi.

decisions.choice: altars for sin ... altars for sinning: a play on one word
alternatives: the more altars, the more sinning (both phrases in the same sense)
decisions.reason: The same words come twice, but with a turn. Altars were built to deal with sin, by offerings that made peace with God; in Ephraim they have become places where sin is committed. The first phrase can also be read as "altars for sinning" both times: the more altars, the more sin (compare 10:1).

decisions.choice: many altars: worship at many shrines
decisions.reason: The law set one place for sacrifice (Deuteronomy 12:5-14), but the northern kingdom built altars on every hill and shrine (4:13; 10:1; 12:12), many of them for the Baals.

decisions.choice: built many altars (B); to take away sin (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps both phrases close to the Hebrew. Readable makes the play plain by saying what altars were for, following m1; this is the likely reading, not a certain one.

decisions.choice: "chuộc tội ... phạm tội"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on one word for sin and sin offering; Vietnamese keeps the play with two phrases sharing "tội".

records.literal_gloss: I write for him [the] many [things] of my instruction; like a strange thing they are regarded.

en.L: I write for him \q the many [things] of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction; \q they are regarded as a strange thing.
en.B: Though I write down for him \q the many things of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} instruction, \q they are treated as something foreign.
en.R: Even if I wrote down for Ephraim \q thousands of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} teachings, \q they would treat them as something foreign.

es.L: Le escribo \q la multitud de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción; \q es considerada como cosa extraña.
es.B: Aunque le escribo \q las muchas cosas de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} instrucción, \q las tratan como algo extranjero.
es.R: Aunque le escribiera a Efraín \q miles de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} enseñanzas, \q las tratarían como algo extranjero.

ko.L: 내가 그를 위하여 \q 내 가르침의 많은 [것을] 기록해도, \q 그들은 그것을 낯선 것으로 여긴다.
ko.B: 내가 그를 위하여 \q 내 가르침을 많이 적어 주어도, \q 그들은 그것을 낯선 것으로 여긴다.
ko.R: 내가 에브라임을 위하여 \q 내 가르침을 수천 가지나 적어 준다 해도, \q 그들은 그것을 낯선 것으로 여길 것이다.

fr.L: J’écris pour lui \q les nombreuses [choses] de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} loi ; \q elles sont considérées comme une chose étrangère.
fr.B: Même si j’écris pour lui \q les nombreux préceptes de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} instruction, \q on les traite comme quelque chose d’étranger.
fr.R: Même si j’écrivais pour Éphraïm \q des milliers de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} enseignements, \q ils les traiteraient comme quelque chose d’étranger.

vi.L: Ta viết cho nó \q vô số [điều] của lời dạy dỗ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q chúng bị xem như điều xa lạ.
vi.B: Dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} viết cho nó \q vô số điều trong lời dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q chúng vẫn bị xem như điều xa lạ.
vi.R: Dù {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} có viết cho Ép-ra-im \q hàng ngàn lời dạy của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q chúng cũng sẽ xem những lời ấy như điều xa lạ.

sw.L: Ninamwandikia \q mambo mengi ya sheria {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q yanahesabiwa kama kitu kigeni.
sw.B: Ingawa ninamwandikia \q mambo mengi ya mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q yanachukuliwa kama kitu kigeni.
sw.R: Hata kama ningemwandikia Efraimu \q maelfu ya mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q wangeyaona kama kitu kigeni.

decisions.choice: the many things of my instruction
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is written one way and read another, with a small difference in the word: the written form means "ten thousand", and the form read aloud means "the many things" or "great numbers". Either way the LORD's instruction is plentiful and detailed, and still rejected.

decisions.choice: I write for him: though I write
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "I wrote", "I write" or "were I to write". Whatever form the instruction takes, past or future, Israel treats it as foreign. "Him" is Ephraim (verse 11).

decisions.choice: regarded as a strange thing: treated as foreign, as if it came from a god they did not know
decisions.reason: The word "strange" is the one used of "strangers" and foreigners in 7:9 and 8:7. Israel treats its own God's instruction as foreign, while it welcomes the foreign nations who devour it.

decisions.choice: Though I write (B); Even if I wrote ... thousands (R); teachings (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the verse sets the abundance of the instruction against its rejection (m2). Readable says "thousands" for the many things, names Ephraim, and says "teachings" for *torah*, as Isaiah sets.

source.text: זִבְחֵ֣י הַבְהָבַ֗י יִזְבְּח֤וּ בָשָׂר֙ וַיֹּאכֵ֔לוּ יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֣א רָצָ֑ם עַתָּ֞ה יִזְכֹּ֤ר עֲוֺנָם֙ וְיִפְקֹ֣ד חַטֹּאותָ֔ם הֵ֖מָּה מִצְרַ֥יִם יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [As] sacrifices of my gifts they sacrifice meat and eat; Yahweh does not accept them; now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins; they to Egypt will return.

en.L: [As] the sacrifices of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} gifts they sacrifice meat and eat [it]; \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is not pleased with them; \q now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remember their iniquity and will punish their sins; \q they will return [to] Egypt.
en.B: They offer sacrifices as gifts to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and eat the meat, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not accept them. \q Now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remember their guilt and punish their sins; \q they will go back to Egypt.
en.R: They offer animals as sacrifices to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and then eat the meat, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not accept them. \q Now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will remember the wrong they have done and make them pay for their sins. \q They will go back to Egypt.

es.L: [Como] sacrificios de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ofrendas sacrifican carne y [la] comen; \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no se complace en ellos; \q ahora {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recordará su iniquidad y castigará sus pecados; \q ellos volverán [a] Egipto.
es.B: Ofrecen sacrificios como ofrendas para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y se comen la carne, \q pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no los acepta. \q Ahora {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recordará su culpa y castigará sus pecados; \q volverán a Egipto.
es.R: Ofrecen animales en sacrificio para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} y luego se comen la carne, \q pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no los acepta. \q Ahora {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} recordará el mal que han hecho y les hará pagar por sus pecados. \q Volverán a Egipto.

ko.L: 그들이 나에게 드리는 예물의 제사로 고기를 바치고 [그것을] 먹는다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들을 기뻐하지 않으신다. \q 이제 그분께서 그들의 죄악을 기억하시고 그들의 죄를 벌하실 것이다. \q 그들은 이집트로 돌아갈 것이다.
ko.B: 그들은 나에게 예물로 제사를 드리고 그 고기를 먹는다. \q 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그것을 받지 않으신다. \q 이제 그분께서 그들의 죄악을 기억하시고 그들의 죄를 벌하실 것이다. \q 그들은 이집트로 돌아갈 것이다.
ko.R: 그들은 짐승을 나에게 제물로 바치고 그 고기를 먹는다. \q 그러나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그것을 받지 않으신다. \q 이제 그분께서 그들이 저지른 잘못을 기억하시고 그 죄의 값을 치르게 하실 것이다. \q 그들은 이집트로 돌아갈 것이다.

fr.L: [Comme] sacrifices de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} dons ils sacrifient de la viande et [la] mangent ; \q {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne les agrée pas ; \q maintenant {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se souviendra de leur iniquité et punira leurs péchés ; \q eux, ils reviendront [en] Égypte.
fr.B: Ils offrent des sacrifices comme des dons pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et en mangent la viande, \q mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne les accepte pas. \q Maintenant {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se souviendra de leur faute et punira leurs péchés ; \q ils reviendront en Égypte.
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}offrent des animaux en sacrifice, puis ils en mangent la viande, \q mais {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne les accepte pas. \q Maintenant {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} va se souvenir du mal qu’ils ont fait et leur faire payer leurs péchés. \q Ils reviendront en Égypte.

vi.L: [Như] các sinh tế của lễ vật dâng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chúng dâng thịt rồi ăn [nó]; \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không vui lòng về chúng; \q bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nhớ đến tội ác chúng và trừng phạt tội lỗi chúng; \q chúng sẽ trở về Ai Cập.
vi.B: Chúng dâng sinh tế làm lễ vật cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} rồi ăn thịt, \q nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không chấp nhận chúng. \q Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nhớ lại tội lỗi chúng và trừng phạt tội ác chúng; \q chúng sẽ trở lại Ai Cập.
vi.R: Chúng dâng thú vật làm sinh tế cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} rồi ăn thịt, \q nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} không chấp nhận chúng. \q Bây giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ nhớ lại những điều sai trái chúng đã làm và bắt chúng trả giá cho tội lỗi mình. \q Chúng sẽ trở lại Ai Cập.

sw.L: [Kama] dhabihu za matoleo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} wanachinja nyama na kula [nyama]; \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hapendezwi nazo; \q sasa atakumbuka uovu wao na kuwaadhibu kwa dhambi zao; \q watarudi [hadi] Misri.
sw.B: Wanatoa dhabihu kama zawadi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} na kula nyama, \q lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hazikubali. \q Sasa atakumbuka hatia yao na kuwaadhibu kwa dhambi zao; \q watarudi Misri.
sw.R: Wanatoa wanyama kama dhabihu {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}} kisha wanakula nyama, \q lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hawakubali. \q Sasa atakumbuka mabaya waliyoyatenda na kuwalipiza kwa dhambi zao. \q Watarudi Misri.

decisions.choice: sacrifices of my gifts: the sacrifices given to me
decisions.reason: The word translated "gifts" is found only here, and its meaning is uncertain. It may come from a verb meaning "give", so that these are the offerings given to the LORD. Others read it as from "love": "they love sacrifice".

decisions.choice: they sacrifice meat and eat it: the offerings have become feasts for themselves
decisions.reason: In many offerings, the worshipers ate the meat themselves (Leviticus 7:15; compare Jeremiah 7:21). The sacrifices have become an occasion for a meal, with no loyalty to the LORD behind them (6:6), so he does not accept them.

decisions.choice: they will return to Egypt: the exodus undone
decisions.reason: The LORD brought Israel out of Egypt (11:1; 12:10). Going back there means losing everything the exodus gave: freedom, land and covenant. In 9:3 the threat is Egypt and Assyria together; in 11:5 Hosea says they will not go back to Egypt, but Assyria will rule them. So "Egypt" here stands for a new bondage, wherever it is.

decisions.choice: as gifts to me (B); animals as sacrifices to me (R); guilt (B); their sins (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the first reading of m1. The word for iniquity is "guilt" at Balanced and "sins" at Readable, as set in the prophets. "Return" is "go back".

decisions.choice: "ahora él recordará su iniquidad y castigará sus pecados" (L) and its Balanced and Readable wording
decisions.reason: The line returns in 9:9; each level keeps the same Spanish there.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 … 않으신다", "그분께서 … 기억하시고", with the honorific where the English has deity spans
decisions.reason: Mid-oracle the voice moves from God's "my gifts" to the LORD in the third person; Korean follows the English spans and gives -시- to the third-person LORD.

decisions.choice: "bây giờ Ngài sẽ nhớ đến tội ác chúng và trừng phạt tội lỗi chúng" (L) and its Balanced and Readable forms
decisions.reason: The line is word for word the published Vietnamese of Jeremiah 14:10 at each level, as the English reuses it; 9:9 repeats it.

records.literal_gloss: And has forgotten Israel his Maker and has built palaces, and Judah has multiplied cities fortified; but I will send fire on his cities, and it will devour her strongholds.

en.L: And Israel has forgotten his Maker and has built palaces, \q and Judah has multiplied walled cities; \q but I will send fire on his cities, \q and it will devour her strongholds.
en.B: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, \q and Judah has built many fortified towns. \q But I will send fire on his towns, \q and it will burn up their fortresses.
en.R: The people of Israel have forgotten the God who made them, and they have built palaces. \q The people of Judah have built many towns with strong walls. \q But I will send fire on their towns, \q and it will burn down their fortresses.

es.L: E Israel ha olvidado a su Hacedor y ha edificado palacios, \q y Judá ha multiplicado ciudades amuralladas; \q pero yo enviaré fuego sobre sus ciudades, \q y devorará sus fortalezas.
es.B: Israel ha olvidado a su Hacedor y ha construido palacios, \q y Judá ha construido muchas ciudades fortificadas. \q Pero enviaré fuego sobre sus ciudades, \q y quemará sus fortalezas.
es.R: El pueblo de Israel ha olvidado al Dios que lo hizo, y ha construido palacios. \q El pueblo de Judá ha construido muchas ciudades con murallas fuertes. \q Pero enviaré fuego sobre sus ciudades, \q y quemará sus fortalezas.

ko.L: 이스라엘은 자기를 지은 이를 잊고 궁전들을 지었으며, \q 유다는 성벽 있는 성읍들을 많이 만들었다. \q 그러나 내가 그의 성읍들에 불을 보낼 것이니, \q 그 불이 그 요새들을 삼킬 것이다.
ko.B: 이스라엘은 자기를 지은 이를 잊고 궁전들을 지었으며, \q 유다는 요새 성읍들을 많이 세웠다. \q 그러나 내가 그 성읍들에 불을 보내겠다. \q 그 불이 그들의 요새들을 삼켜 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 이스라엘 백성은 자기들을 지은 하나님을 잊고 궁전들을 지었다. \q 유다 백성은 튼튼한 성벽이 있는 성읍들을 많이 세웠다. \q 그러나 나는 그 성읍들에 불을 보내겠다. \q 그 불이 그들의 요새들을 다 태워 버릴 것이다.

fr.L: Et Israël a oublié son Créateur et il a bâti des palais, \q et Juda a multiplié les villes fortifiées ; \q mais j’enverrai le feu sur ses villes, \q et il dévorera ses forteresses.
fr.B: Israël a oublié son Créateur et il a bâti des palais, \q et Juda a construit beaucoup de villes fortifiées. \q Mais j’enverrai le feu sur ses villes, \q et il dévorera leurs forteresses.
fr.R: Les Israélites ont oublié le Dieu qui les a faits, et ils ont bâti des palais. \q Les gens de Juda ont construit beaucoup de villes aux murs solides. \q Mais j’enverrai le feu sur leurs villes, \q et il brûlera leurs forteresses.

vi.L: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã quên Đấng Tạo Thành mình và xây các cung điện, \q và Giu-đa đã gia tăng các thành kiên cố; \q nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ sai lửa xuống trên các thành nó, \q và lửa sẽ thiêu nuốt các đồn lũy của nó.
vi.B: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã quên Đấng Tạo Thành mình mà xây cất cung điện, \q còn Giu-đa thì xây nhiều thành kiên cố. \q Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giáng lửa trên các thành ấy, \q và lửa sẽ thiêu rụi các đồn lũy của chúng.
vi.R: Dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã quên Đức Chúa Trời là Đấng dựng nên mình, và chúng đã xây các cung điện. \q Dân Giu-đa đã xây nhiều thành có tường vững chắc. \q Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ giáng lửa trên các thành của chúng, \q và lửa sẽ thiêu rụi các đồn lũy của chúng.

sw.L: Na Israeli amemsahau Muumba wake, na amejenga majumba ya kifalme, \q na Yuda ameongeza miji yenye ngome; \q lakini nitatuma moto juu ya miji yake, \q nao utaziteketeza ngome zake.
sw.B: Israeli amemsahau Muumba wake na kujenga majumba ya kifalme, \q na Yuda amejenga miji mingi yenye ngome. \q Lakini nitatuma moto juu ya miji yake, \q nao utaziteketeza ngome zao.
sw.R: Watu wa Israeli wamemsahau Mungu aliyewaumba, nao wamejenga majumba ya kifalme. \q Watu wa Yuda wamejenga miji mingi yenye kuta imara. \q Lakini nitatuma moto juu ya miji yao, \q nao utaziteketeza ngome zao.

decisions.choice: Israel has forgotten his Maker: forgetting God in prosperity
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy warns that when Israel builds fine houses and grows rich, it will forget the LORD (Deuteronomy 8:11-14; 32:18). That is what has happened: the people trust in palaces and walls instead of the God who made them a nation (compare Isaiah 17:10; 22:11).

decisions.choice: palaces: great buildings, perhaps temples
decisions.reason: The word is used both of palaces and of temples. Here, beside fortified cities, it most likely means palaces and great houses, but it may include the shrines of the northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: I will send fire on his cities, and it will devour her strongholds
decisions.reason: Amos uses nearly the same words in his oracles against the nations, Judah and Israel (Amos 1:4, 7, 10, 12, 14; 2:2, 5). "His cities" are Judah's; "her strongholds" may be those of the cities or of the land.

decisions.choice: towns (B, R); their fortresses (B, R); the God who made them (R); the people of Israel, of Judah (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "their" for the shift from "his cities" to "her strongholds", which the Hebrew makes between masculine and feminine forms. Readable says "the God who made them" for "his Maker" and speaks of the people of Israel and Judah.

decisions.choice: "자기를 지은 이" (L, B), "자기들을 지은 하나님" (R), without -시-
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself as Israel's Maker, so the title takes no honorific in his own mouth.
